title: Channels (Web, Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, Slack)
content:
## Overview

Wingman works seamlessly across **Web, Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, and Slack**. Each channel supports text, voice messages, and images, with per-channel message limits and connection flows. You can also accept payments directly in-channel.

All channels share the same Wingman backend—conversations sync across platforms when users link their accounts.

---

## Supported Channels

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Web" icon="globe">
    Embed Wingman as a widget or full-page chat on your site.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Telegram" icon="send">
    Deploy as a Telegram bot; supports groups and channels.
  </Card>
  <Card title="WhatsApp" icon="message-circle">
    Connect via WhatsApp Business API; 24-hour session window applies.
  </Card>
  <Card title="iMessage" icon="message-square">
    iOS-native chat; requires Apple Business Chat approval.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Slack" icon="hash">
    Add Wingman to workspaces as a bot or app.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Message and Voice Limits

Each channel enforces different size and duration caps:

| Channel    | Text message max | Voice message max | Image max |
|------------|------------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Web        | 10,000 chars     | 10 MB / 2 min     | 10 MB     |
| Telegram   | 4,096 chars      | 10 MB / 2 min     | 10 MB     |
| WhatsApp   | 4,096 chars      | 10 MB / 2 min     | 5 MB      |
| iMessage   | 10,000 chars     | 10 MB / 2 min     | 10 MB     |
| Slack      | 4,000 chars      | 10 MB / 2 min     | 10 MB     |

<Note>
Voice messages are automatically transcribed and processed; the 10 MB / 2 min limit applies to the uploaded audio file.
</Note>

---

## Connecting a Channel

<Steps>
  <Step title="Select your channel">
    In the Wingman workspace, go to **Settings → Channels** and choose which platform to connect.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Follow the platform-specific flow">
    - **Web**: Copy the embed snippet and paste into your site's HTML.
    - **Telegram**: Create a bot via BotFather, paste the token into Emergent.
    - **WhatsApp**: Register a WhatsApp Business account, verify your number, and connect via the Meta Business Suite.
    - **iMessage**: Apply for Apple Business Chat, then link your account in Settings.
    - **Slack**: Install the Emergent app from the Slack App Directory and authorize the workspace.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Test the connection">
    Send a test message from the channel; you should see it appear in the Wingman **Inbox** within seconds.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Warning title="WhatsApp 24-hour window">
After a user's last message, you have **24 hours** to reply freely. Outside that window, you can only send **pre-approved message templates** (configured in Meta Business Suite). Plan proactive outreach accordingly.
</Warning>

---

## In-Channel Payments

Wingman supports checkout flows directly inside messaging apps:

- **Telegram**: Payment bots via Telegram Payments (Stripe, PayPal).
- **WhatsApp**: Send a payment link; user completes checkout in-browser.
- **Web widget**: Inline Stripe or PayPal checkout modal.
- **Slack / iMessage**: Payment links open externally.

Configure payment providers in **Settings → Payments**. See [Payment methods & regional billing](/payment-methods-regional-billing) for details.

<Tip>
Telegram and Web channels offer the smoothest in-app payment experience; WhatsApp and iMessage redirect to a browser.
</Tip>

---

## Permission Prompts

Certain Wingman actions trigger **per-channel permission prompts** the first time a user invokes them:

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Location sharing">
    Wingman may ask "Share your location?" if the skill requires geo-data. Users approve once; preference is remembered per channel.
  </Accordion>
  
  <Accordion title="Camera / microphone (Web only)">
    Browser-based permissions appear when Wingman requests a photo or live voice recording.
  </Accordion>
  
  <Accordion title="Notification preferences">
    On Telegram and Slack, users can mute/unmute Wingman's proactive messages. WhatsApp notifications follow the OS contact-notification settings.
  </Accordion>
  
  <Accordion title="Contact sync (optional)">
    If Wingman offers to remember contacts (e.g. "Add John to your directory"), the user confirms once.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

<Info>
Emergent never stores sensitive data (like raw voice files or exact GPS) beyond the lifetime of a single request unless the user explicitly grants storage permission.
</Info>

---

## Channel-Specific Considerations

### Telegram
- Supports **groups and channels**: Wingman can respond to @mentions or all messages (configure in bot settings).
- Rich media: stickers, polls, and inline keyboards work natively.

### WhatsApp
- **24-hour session window**: after that, only template messages are allowed.
- Number verification required via Meta; approval can take 1–2 business days.

### iMessage
- Requires **Apple Business Chat** approval (stricter vetting).
- Best for customer support; less suited for high-volume broadcast.

### Slack
- Appears as a bot in channels or DMs.
- Slash commands (`/wingman help`) can trigger shortcuts.

### Web
- Fully customizable widget appearance (colors, avatar, placement).
- No platform approval needed—deploy instantly.

---

## Syncing Conversations Across Channels

When a user links their Telegram, WhatsApp, and Web accounts (via email or phone number), Wingman **unifies the conversation history**:

1. User chats on Telegram, then continues on Web.
2. Wingman recognizes the same user and retrieves context.
3. The **Inbox** shows a single threaded conversation across all channels.

<Note>
Account linking is optional but recommended for a seamless experience. Users initiate linking by verifying their contact details in any channel.
</Note>
